findings.quote: a gulf some call by one name and most call the Bargylian Gulf, after the cities built around its inner recess
findings.problem: The Greek reads προσαγορευομένῳ ***, παρὰ δὲ τοῖς πλείστοις Βαργυλιητικῷ: the gulf's first name is lost in a lacuna (***). The English smooths the gap into 'some call by one name'. Greek says only that it is called [name lost], but by most the Bargylietic gulf, a name shared with the cities (συνωνύμως) at its head.
findings.proposed_fix: a gulf called *** [name lost in the Greek] but by most the Bargylian Gulf, a name shared with the cities built around its inner recess

findings.quote: never know how to stop opposing and resenting such declarations by historians throughout my whole work
findings.problem: οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅπως ... ἐναντιούμενος καὶ δυσανασχετῶν διατελῶ: 'I do not know how it is, but I continually find myself opposing and resenting'. οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅπως is an idiom for 'somehow'; it does not mean 'I do not know how to stop'.
findings.proposed_fix: somehow find myself, throughout my whole work, opposing and resenting such declarations by historians

units.note: Also, 'ten stades in circuit': Greek has only τὸ μέγεθος τῆς πόλεώς ἐστι δέκα στάδια ('the size of the city is ten stades'); 'in circuit' is an addition, but the sense is probably right, so not flagged.

findings.quote: and become altogether deep and unfordable.
findings.problem: The Greek ends the Alpheus passage with παντελῶς ἄβατος ὢν καὶ βαρύς. *** : a lacuna follows. The English reads on as if the passage were complete.
findings.proposed_fix: and become altogether deep and unfordable. [Text lost here in the Greek.]

findings.quote: seized the high ground on the right
findings.problem: προκαταλαβόμενος τοὺς ὑπερδεξίους τόπους: 'having first occupied the commanding (overlooking) positions'. ὑπερδέξιος means advantageous high ground, not ground on the right; no side is stated (cf. ch. 18, τοὺς ὑπερκειμένους τῶν πολεμίων τόπους).
